proved_step: LEMMA (dim-2 slice, tw=0): Let C subset GF(3)^n be a 2-dim code with no zero coordinate, G a 2 x n generator matrix with columns c_j. A simple rank-2 matroid with >=3 points is connected, so disconnection forces exactly two points. Scope: dim 2, no zero coordinate, tw=0 only. proved_step: REPAIRED LEMMA (any dimension k): Let C subset GF(3)^n be a k-dim code with no zero coordinate, with columns c_1..c_n of a generator matrix G (k x n). Rank k forces all k points to occur and to be independent. Conversely an edgeless graph on k vertices has tw 0 and any tw-0 graph is edgeless. Dim 2 case is the earlier lemma restated (2 independent points = disconnected rank-2 matroid with 2 points). Scope: all k, tw=0 only, GF(3). proved_step: LEMMA A (tw=0 characterisation, any k, GF(3)): for a code C of dimension k with no zero coordinate and generator columns c_j, min over bases B of tw(G_B) = 0 iff the projective points of the c_j are exactly k points forming a basis of GF(3)^k. PROOF: for a basis change A (rows of A G), column j has support T_j = supp(A c_j) and G_B is the union of cliques on the T_j. So G_B is edgeless iff |T_j| <= 1 for all j, i.e. every A c_j is a nonzero multiple of a unit vector; full rank k forces the k unit vectors to occur, so the points are k independent points. Conversely, such points are sent to unit vectors by A. LEMMA B (clique lower bound, any k): for every basis B, tw(G_B) >= max_j |T_j| - 1, since each T_j is a clique and tw(K_s) = s - 1 with tw monotone under subgraphs; hence min_B tw(G_B) >= min_A max_j |supp(A c_j)| - 1. Scope: GF(3), no zero coordinate, coefficient graph = rows adjacent iff supports share a coordinate.

Proof: tw<=1 iff G_A not K3; a column with support size 3 forces K3; support size <=2 for all columns iff S lies in H_1 u H_2 u H_3 (the non-concurrent lines with normals = rows of A); the pair {r,s} occurs iff some point of S is private to H_t; so K3 iff every H_t has a private point. Two-line covers give tw<=1 via a third line M not through L cap L'; conversely no private point on H_t forces S in H_r u H_s. Consequence: min tw = 0 iff S is 3 independent points (234 sets), = 1 iff two-line cover, else = 2. Scope: k=3, GF(3). Does not close G0001.

proved_step: LEMMA U (upper bound, width theorem). Setting as in the owner lower-bound text (steps i-iv, S0009). Let (T,beta) be a tree decomposition of G of width k = tw(G). Let tau1 = (1,2,0) and tau2 = (0,1,2) in T (both sum to 0 mod 3; independent; their supports {1,2} and {2,3} meet in colour 2). For v in V and i in {1,2}, let b(v,i) in K_G be the element whose vertex part is tau_i at v and 0 elsewhere; its edge part is forced by k(e,c) = -(k(u,c)+k(w,c)). Restriction to vertex coordinates is an isomorphism K_G -> T^V, and the vertex parts of the b(v,i) form a basis of T^V, so B_T = (b(v,i)) is a basis of K_G. Support of b(v,i): coordinates (v,c) and (e,c) for edges e at v, with c in supp tau_i. Two basis vectors share a coordinate iff (a) they have the same vertex v (they share (v,2)), or (b) their vertices u,v are adjacent in G (they share (uv,c) for c in supp tau_i meet supp tau_j, nonempty by L2); nonadjacent distinct vertices share nothing. Hence H_{B_T} = G x K2 (strong product: each vertex blown up to a 2-clique, adjacent blocks fully joined). Tree decomposition of H_{B_T}: replace each bag beta(t) by beta(t) x {1,2}. Each (v,i) lies in exactly the nodes containing v (connected). An in-block edge lies in the bag of v. A cross edge (u,i)(v,j) with uv in E lies in some beta(t) containing u and v, hence in beta(t) x {1,2}. The width is at most 2(k+1)-1 = 2k+1. So min over bases of tw(H_B) <= 2tw(G)+1. With the owner lower bound (every basis has tw(H_B) >= 2tw(G)+1), w*(F(G)) = min_B tw(H_B) = 2tw(G)+1 exactly, relative to the spec's definition of tw(H_B). LEMMA H (upper bound, basis coefficient graph). Let G be a finite graph, k = tw(G), tau_1=(1,2,0), tau_2=(0,1,2) over GF(3)^3, and B_T = {b(v,i)} as in S0018 (vertex part tau_i at v; edge part -tau_i on edges at v). (a) The coefficient graph H_{B_T} equals the lexicographic product G[K_2]: vertex coordinates (v,c) are shared only by b(v,1),b(v,2), which share colour 1 since supp tau_1 and supp tau_2 both contain 1; edge coordinates (uv,c) are shared by b(u,i),b(v,j) iff c in supp tau_i and c in supp tau_j, which is nonempty for all i,j; no other shared coordinates. (b) Bag doubling: for an optimal tree decomposition (T,beta) of G of width k, beta'(x) = beta(x) x {1,2} is a tree decomposition of G[K_2]: bag size <= 2(k+1); the pairs (v,1),(v,2) lie together in any bag containing v; for uv in E the four pairs lie together in any bag containing u and v; for each (v,i) the bags containing it form the same subtree as for v. Hence tw(H_{B_T}) <= 2tw(G)+1. Scope: upper bound only, for the specific basis B_T; the equality min_B tw(H_B) = 2tw(G)+1 still needs the owner's lower bound (steps i-iv), which is not checked here. statement: For every finite simple graph G, tw(G[K_2]) = 2*tw(G)+1, where G[K_2] has vertex set V x {0,1} and (a,i)~(b,j) iff ab in E(G) or (a=b and i!=j). SCOPE: this is a statement about the fixed graph G[K_2] only. It does NOT bound min over bases of the coefficient graph of K_G, so it does not close G0001 or S0018.
derivation: UPPER BOUND: let (T,beta) be a tree decomposition of G of width k=tw(G). Set beta'(t)=beta(t) x {0,1}. Every edge (a,i)(b,j) of H has a=b (then a in beta(t) for some t, so both ends lie in beta'(t)) or ab in E (then a,b lie in a common bag). For each a, {t : (a,i) in beta'(t)} = {t : a in beta(t)} is connected, so beta' is a tree decomposition of H with bags of size at most 2(k+1), i.e. width at most 2k+1. LOWER BOUND: by Seymour-Thomas take a bramble B of G of order k+1. Let F = {B x {i} : B in B, i in {0,1}}. Each B x {i} is connected in H (edges (a,i)(b,i) for ab in E). Two members touch: if B, B' share a vertex a, then (a,i) and (a,j) lie in them and are equal or adjacent; if B, B' are joined by an edge ab of G with a in B, b in B', then (a,i) ~ (b,j) in H for any i,j. So F is a bramble of H. If X hits every member of F, then X_i = {v : (v,i) in X} hits every B in B for i=0 and i=1, so |X_i| >= k+1 and |X| >= 2(k+1). Hence the bramble order of H is at least 2k+2, and by Seymour-Thomas tw(H) >= 2k+1. Both bounds together give tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1. The same argument gives tw(G[K_n]) >= n(tw(G)+1)-1 with the matching upper bound by n-fold bag blow-up. STATUS: CLAIMED; the author is claude-haiku-5-5 and cannot review its own step. Finite evidence: cm-7cde1dde06454301 (n<=5, 1099 graphs, exact) and cm-1a3bfa59750945e3 (8 graphs, n=6).

proved_step: LEMMA W-F (width theorem over an arbitrary field F). Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph, V nonempty, and let K_G^F subset F^I be the homogeneous kernel: (V) k(v,1)+k(v,2)+k(v,3)=0 for all v; (E) k(e,c)=-(k(u,c)+k(w,c)) for e={u,w}, all c. Then min over all bases B of K_G^F of tw(H_B) = 2 tw(G)+1, where H_B is the coefficient graph (j~k iff some coordinate is nonzero in both b_j and b_k). PROOF. Lower bound: the owner's Steps (i)-(iv) (LOWER_BOUND_PROOF.md, sec. 1) go through verbatim over F. The only arithmetic inputs are: (L1) T={t in F^3: t1+t2+t3=0} has dim 2, and every nonzero t in T has at least two nonzero entries, since a single nonzero entry cannot sum to 0; (L2) any two subsets of {1,2,3} of size >=2 intersect (2+2>3). Steps (i)-(iv) use only these, linear algebra, and Fact (C). Hence tw(H_B) >= 2 tw(G)+1 for every basis B. Upper bound: put tau1=(1,-1,0), tau2=(0,1,-1) in T. Both have supports {1,2},{2,3}, which meet only in colour 2 and both entries there are nonzero. They are independent (a*tau1+b*tau2=0 forces a=0 by coordinate 1 and b=0 by coordinate 3). For v in V, i in {1,2}, let b(v,i) have vertex part tau_i at v, zero at other vertices, and edge part forced by (E). Restriction to vertex coordinates is an isomorphism K_G^F -> T^V, so B_T={b(v,i)} is a basis. Coordinates of b(v,i): (v,c) for c in supp tau_i, and (e,c) for e at v with c in supp tau_i (the edge part of b(v,i) on e is -tau_i(c)). Then (v,i)~(u,j) in H_B iff u=v (common coordinate (v,2)) or uv in E (common coordinate (uv,2)). Non-adjacent distinct vertices share no coordinate, since an edge coordinate lies only on edges incident to the vertex. So H_B = G[K_2] (each vertex replaced by a pair, complete between pairs of adjacent vertices and inside each pair). For a tree decomposition (T,beta) of G of width k, the bags beta(t) x {1,2} form a tree decomposition of H_B of width 2(k+1)-1 = 2k+1. So min_B tw(H_B) <= 2 tw(G)+1. Together with the lower bound: min_B tw(H_B) = 2 tw(G)+1. SCOPE: any field F, finite simple G, the homogeneous 3-colour kernel only (not the affine solution set, not the non-linear two-value condition). ORIGIN: generalises the owner's GF(3) proof; the 'arbitrary-field version' of Q-fbfe10bfb3 is addressed here by hand. Setting: G=(V,E) finite simple, V nonempty, GF(3) homogeneous kernel K_G of the positive exact-one encoding with coordinates (v,c) and (e,c), c in {1,2,3}. Let tau_1=(1,2,0), tau_2=(0,1,2) in T (sum-zero vectors). Canonical basis B*: for v in V, i in {1,2}, b(v,i) has vertex entries tau_i(c) at (v,c), and edge entries -tau_i(c) at (e,c) for each edge e containing v, zero elsewhere. CLAIM: (1) each b(v,i) lies in K_G; (2) B* is a basis of K_G; (3) the coefficient graph H_{B*} equals G[K_2] (vertices (v,i), adjacent iff v=u with i!=j, or uv in E); (4) hence min over bases of tw(H_B) <= tw(G[K_2]) <= 2 tw(G)+1. PROOF. (1) Vertex sums of tau_i are 0. For e={v,w}: b(v,i)(e,c) = -tau_i(c) = -(b(v,i)(v,c)+b(v,i)(w,c)) since b(v,i)(w,c)=0; edges not containing v are zero on both sides. (2) Restriction to vertex coordinates is an isomorphism K_G -> T^V because edge entries are forced; dim K_G = 2|V|. Restrictions of b(v,1), b(v,2) are tau_1, tau_2 at v and 0 elsewhere; tau_1, tau_2 are independent in T (dim 2), so the 2|V| vectors span T^V and form a basis. (3) supp tau_1={1,2}, supp tau_2={2,3}; both contain colour 2. Same vertex v: share (v,2), adjacent. uv in E: b(v,i) and b(u,j) are both nonzero at (e,2), adjacent. Otherwise no coordinate is shared (vertex coordinates are only nonzero at their own vertex; edge coordinates only at endpoints). So H_{B*} = G[K_2]. (4) Take a width-tw(G) tree decomposition (T,beta); set beta'(t)=beta(t) x {1,2}. Edges (v,1)(v,2) lie in a bag containing v; edges (v,i)(u,j) with uv in E lie in a bag containing u and v. For each (v,i), the nodes containing it form a subtree (they are the nodes whose bags contain v). Max bag size is 2(tw(G)+1), so width <= 2tw(G)+1. QED.
